tracks.publicName: Expunging a case that was dismissed or ended in a not guilty verdict

controllingAuthority.summary: Where an acquittal was entered for all criminal charges, or all criminal charges were otherwise dismissed, the court shall enter an order expunging the district court record. Expunge means the record becomes a confidential record exempt from public access under § 22.7; nothing is destroyed.

exclusions: Dismissals related to a deferred judgment under § 907.9, which route to the deferred-judgment track.
Cases dismissed because the defendant was found not guilty by reason of insanity.
Cases in which the defendant was found incompetent to stand trial.
Matters that are not public offenses as defined in § 692.1.
Appellate records, other than appeals of simple misdemeanors to district court, under Rule 2.84(5).
Partial dispositions. All charges in the separately numbered case must be acquitted or dismissed.

tracks.legalName: Application to Expunge Misdemeanor Court Records under Iowa Code section 901C.3

controllingAuthority.summary: One misdemeanor conviction may be expunged per lifetime, more than eight years after the date of conviction, where financial obligations are paid, no criminal charges are pending, and the defendant has not previously been granted two deferred judgments. The court shall enter the order as a matter of law on proof; the burden is expressly on the defendant.

exclusions: Section 901C.3(2) excludes twenty-four categories, which must be built from the statute rather than from the form's note: (a) § 123.46; (b) a simple misdemeanor under § 123.47(3) or a similar local ordinance; (c) §§ 321.218, 321A.32, 321J.21; (d) § 321J.2; (e) a sex offense as defined in § 692A.101; (f) involuntary manslaughter under § 707.5; (g) assault under § 708.2(3); (h) § 708.2A; (i) harassment under § 708.7; (j) stalking under § 708.11; (k) removal of an officer's communication or control device under § 708.12; (l) trespass under § 716.8(3) or (4); (m) chapter 717C; (n) chapter 719; (o) chapter 720; (p) § 721.2; (q) § 721.10; (r) § 723.1; (s) chapter 724; (t) chapter 726; (u) chapter 728; (v) chapter 901A; (w) a comparable offense listed in 49 C.F.R. § 383.51(b) table 1 or § 383.51(e) table 4; (x) a conviction under prior law of an offense comparable to an offense enumerated in this subsection.
Paragraphs (w) and (x) are absent from the official form's note and from both internal references.
Section 235B.20 appears on the official form's note but is not in the Iowa Code 2026 text; screen it out and refer until resolved.
One expungement under this section per lifetime.
Any pending charge of a public offense as defined in § 692.1.
Two previously granted deferred judgments, counted per Rule 2.83(5).

controllingAuthority.summary: A conviction for consumption or intoxication in public places under § 123.46, or a similar local ordinance, shall be expunged two years after the conviction where there are no criminal convictions in the intervening two years other than local traffic violations or simple misdemeanour violations under chapter 321. Court debt is expressly not a precondition.

exclusions: A criminal conviction during the two-year period following the conviction, other than a local traffic violation or a simple misdemeanour violation under chapter 321.

waitingPeriods.duration: Two years, with no disqualifying intervening conviction inside that window

tracks.legalName: Application to Expunge Possession of Alcohol under the Legal Age Court Records under Iowa Code section 123.47

controllingAuthority.summary: A conviction under § 123.47(3), possession of alcohol under the legal age, or a similar local ordinance, shall be expunged as a matter of law two years after conviction with a clean intervening record. Section 123.47(9) additionally requires removal from Department of Public Safety criminal history data files after clerk notice, and provides that an expunged conviction is not a prior offence for enhancement under § 123.47(4) unless the new violation occurred before entry of the expungement order.

exclusions: Convictions under § 123.47 generally rather than subsection 3 specifically.
A criminal conviction during the two-year period other than a local traffic violation or a simple misdemeanour under chapter 321.

waitingPeriods.duration: Two years, with no disqualifying intervening conviction inside that window

tracks.legalName: Expungement of a Deferred Judgment Record on Discharge from Probation
tracks.publicName: Clearing a deferred judgment after probation

controllingAuthority.summary: On discharge from probation where judgment was deferred under § 907.3, the court's criminal record with reference to the deferred judgment shall be expunged, together with dismissed counts in the same charging instrument and other related dismissed charges arising from the same transaction or occurrence or a common scheme or plan. The record is not expunged until financial obligations in that case are paid. The deferred judgment itself remains on the state court administrator's deferred judgment docket and is not expunged. This mechanism sits outside Rules 2.80 through 2.86 and has no Rule 2.86 form.

exclusions: A revoked deferred judgment. Revocation makes the case ineligible under chapter 907; the resulting conviction may then be eligible under § 901C.3 if it is a misdemeanour.
Cases where financial obligations in the case containing the deferred judgment remain unpaid.

waitingPeriods.condition: Discharge from probation, with all financial obligations in that case paid

units.label: Verify that the automatic expungement happened, and diagnose it if it did not
units.description: For a discharge after July 1, 2013 there is no participant filing: the expungement is expected to occur without an application. The product is diagnostic. Confirm the disposition was a deferred judgment rather than a conviction or a dismissal, confirm discharge and its date, confirm every financial obligation in that case is paid, check whether the case still appears on the public online docket, and if it does, contact the clerk of the district court for that county. The usual blocker is an unpaid balance in that case, which is actionable.

units.label: Application for a discharge predating July 1, 2013
units.description: For a discharge before July 1, 2013 an application is required, but no statewide form exists, no rule governs it, and the statutory mechanics are thin. The filing vehicle is legally unresolved, so no packet is generated and no strategy is invented.
units.unavailableReason: The correct mechanism for a pre-July-1-2013 deferred judgment expungement request is unresolved: no form, no rule. A custom pleading would be speculative.

geography.venue: Iowa District Court for the county of the case containing the deferred judgment.

destination.name: Clerk of the Iowa District Court for the county of the case
destination.detail: For a post-2013 discharge the participant contacts the clerk where the record still appears on the public docket. For a pre-2013 discharge the mechanism is unresolved.

components.notes: Diagnostic sequence and clerk-contact instructions for a post-July-2013 discharge, plus the balance check that is the usual blocker.

tracks.legalName: Iowa Division of Criminal Investigation Criminal History Record Check on Form DCI-77
tracks.publicName: Getting the DCI criminal history record check you need to file

controllingAuthority.summary: Rule 2.81(2) requires an official Division of Criminal Investigation Iowa criminal history record check, obtained by submitting form DCI-77 with a release authorization signature and dated within the past 30 days, as a component of a § 901C.3 misdemeanour expungement application. It retrieves and verifies records; it does not alter, seal, expunge or correct one.

exclusions: This is not relief. It alters no record and must not be counted as a paid packet mechanism or a substantive relief mechanism.

waitingPeriods.condition: Not applicable. The check must be dated within 30 days of filing the § 901C.3 application
